openings.claim: Refine parent A by filing shelf holds consistently under the reservation holder's surname within the existing divider-card regions. This could help readers and the evening clerk retrieve the correct available hold promptly while keeping identities behind the desk; no benefit has been demonstrated.
openings.delta: The cards retain their search-narrowing function, but household-member surnames cease to determine the shelf region. Correcting placement strengthens the existing mechanism without adding another location-recording mechanism.
openings.prediction: If household misfiling contributes materially to delays, normalized shelf holds will require fewer second-region searches and shorter retrievals. Cart encounters and delays from changed locations need not improve; the all-pickup 95% threshold remains unproven.
openings.rival_prediction: The nearest alternative explanation is that changing locations and peak demand dominate delays. It predicts little improvement in complete encounter times after surname normalization, even when shelf-region searches become more accurate.
openings.defeat: A comparison showing unchanged shelf search times and second-region searches after confirmed household misfilings are corrected would defeat the proposed retrieval benefit. Preparation exceeding ten clerk-minutes would defeat operational feasibility under the original constraints.
openings.probe: Propose a bounded behind-desk dry-retrieval comparison using the existing clerk, divider cards, paper and timing sheet, before and after correcting identified household misfilings. Count all preparation, corrections and probe work toward ten clerk-minutes and stop at the cap. Use the existing shelves and cart; expose no reader details and perform no experimental handoffs. This tests retrieval function only, not full pickup success.
assumptions: Existing behind-desk labels or records identify the reservation holder accurately; this capability is unconfirmed.
Useful corrections and paired retrievals fit alongside routine preparation within ten clerk-minutes; O6 leaves only two minutes on the stipulated sampled day.
A subsequent full-window evaluation would need complete pickup times and correct-reader verification; this probe cannot establish 95% within two minutes or zero wrong-reader handoffs.
